clue.text: Scottish isle, for example, rejected small plans

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone's island holiday plans, to Arran perhaps, were turned down for being too modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' describes the isle in the surface, but it is a piece of its own; 'rejected' sends it backwards. 'plans' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to organise or set it up in advance, a synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Make-up uneven, hard to remove close to bedtime

indicators.note: says the letter for hard is to be taken out of the word before it

parts.note: an uneven surface is a rough one
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the end of bedtime

explanation.surface: Uneven make-up that is hard to take off at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove' drops H from ROUGH, leaving ROUG; 'close to' supplies the last letter of 'bedtime'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a red cosmetic for the cheeks, one kind of make-up.

clue.text: Nice store designed with gold front — they sell lots

indicators.note: says the gold goes at the front of the rest

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: something designed has been planned and laid out anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop in Nice laid out with a golden frontage, staffed by salespeople.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' signals the shuffle of 'Nice store'; 'front' puts the gold symbol first. 'lots' are items at a sale, not a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale by bidding, each item is a lot, and the people running the sale knock them down to buyers.

clue.text: One in pack touching yellow marginally during game

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these letters go inside the game

parts.note: golf is a game played with clubs
RE means concerning, about, touching on

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its outer letters, here the first and last of yellow

explanation.surface: A golfer barely touches the yellow ball mid-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marginally' means only the edge letters of 'yellow' are used, and 'during' sets them, with the word for touching, inside the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey wolf hunts in packs, so it is an example of an animal found in a pack.

clue.text: Deputy back home with business minutes also

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back or support it
someone at home is in
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
MM, doubling M, is a plural abbreviation for minutes, as pp is for pages
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A deputy supports a home office business while minutes are taken too.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy ranks next below the leader and takes over when they are absent.

clue.text: Type of Bible from God in spirit

indicators.note: says the Latin phrase sits inside the spirit

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic spirit
Deo is Latin for from or by God, as in Deo gratias

explanation.surface: A sort of Bible that comes straight from God in spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from God' is a Latin ablative, as in Deo gratias; 'in' sets it inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gideons are a Christian group that leave free Bibles in hotel rooms, so those copies are named after them.

clue.text: Launch publication around spring

indicators.note: turned around, so the combined letters read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw or launch something high
a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: Launching a new magazine around springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LOBMAG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring about is to leap playfully, which is the verb sense here, like a lamb frolicking.

clue.text: I've been stupid to cheat on husband

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or cheat them
H is the abbreviation for husband in family records

explanation.surface: A spouse confesses to the folly of cheating on their husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've been stupid' stands for the whole exclamation, which can replace the interjection in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation popularised by Homer Simpson is said when realising one has blundered.

clue.text: Old fellows arrived with artist unseen by TV viewers

parts.note: FF is the plural abbreviation of F for fellow
came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Elderly men and a painter turn up at a studio but stay out of shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening away from the lens is not broadcast, so the audience at home cannot see it.

clue.text: After brief fast, chap filled savoury tart

indicators.note: says the chap comes after the shortened word
a brief word is cut short, so its last letter goes

parts.note: quick means fast
he is any male, a chap

explanation.surface: After a short fast, a man tucked into a savoury tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the last letter; 'After' sets the chap behind. 'filled' looks like a verb for eating but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This French dish is a pastry case filled with an egg custard and savoury ingredients.

clue.text: In the morning, mum in fact damaged part of engine

indicators.note: says the morning and silence letters go inside the rearranged word
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
mum, as in keep mum, means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Mum damaged the car one morning, a fact about a broken engine part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother but the word for keeping quiet; 'damaged' shuffles 'fact', and 'in' holds the morning and the hush inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is a rotating rod with cams that opens and closes the valves of a motor.

clue.text: Type of house embraced by boss emigrating

indicators.note: embraced by means held within, so the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: A boss emigrating takes along a style of house.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'boSS EMIgrating'.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house shares one wall with its neighbour, a common British home type.

clue.text: Place to rest nosh on computer system

indicators.note: in an across entry one part placed on another comes after it

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's computer operating system
to nosh is to eat

explanation.surface: Somewhere to settle with a snack and the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bench or seat built into a window recess is somewhere to sit and relax.

clue.text: Stunted trees etc over spring become attractive when groomed

parts.note: scrub is vegetation of stunted trees and bushes
up means over, finished, as in time's up
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Stunted bushes after spring look lovely once tidied.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means someone looks good once washed and smartened, as after a tidy-up.

clue.text: Left crook back on street somewhere in south Wales

indicators.note: in an across entry the reversed word sits on, after, the street

parts.note: a lane is a street

indicators.note: back means the letters are read the other way

parts.note: crook is Australian slang for ill

explanation.surface: A criminal leaves, returning to a Welsh street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ILL into LLI. 'crook' looks like a criminal, but in Australian slang it means sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in Carmarthenshire, in the south of Wales.

clue.text: Green character Alfie roamed headland

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: An environmentalist named Alfie wandered over a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roamed' turns ALFIE into LEAFI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being leafy means being full of foliage, so the quality is a green nature.

clue.text: Smell river — that's awful!

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
eek is a cry of alarm or disgust

explanation.surface: Someone reacts in horror to the stench of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to stink, giving off a strong smell.

clue.text: Mint Brenda munched touring north and west

indicators.note: something touring a place goes around it, so the rearranged letters surround the compass letter
munched means chewed up, so these letters are mashed into a new order

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Brenda chewed a mint while travelling the north and west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'munched' turns BRENDA into BRANDE; 'touring' wraps it round N to give BRANDNE.
explanation.definitionFit: In mint condition means unused and new, like a coin fresh from the press.

clue.text: Long depression needing fifth beer

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A prolonged low mood that calls for a fifth pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits but means a dip in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale is a valley, a long hollow in the landscape.

clue.text: Brainy Anglican relative wins cups

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

indicators.note: to win something is to take it in, so the relative holds the cups

parts.note: a bra has cups

explanation.surface: A clever churchgoer's relative wins trophies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like trophies but means the cups of a bra, which 'wins' takes inside the relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means intellectual, appealing to the intellect.

clue.text: Preoccupy unknown character that's put in car key

indicators.note: says the unknown goes inside the car

parts.note: a Fiat is an Italian car
X is the algebraic unknown
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An unknown person is busy putting a key into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets X inside FIAT, giving FIXAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To fixate someone is to make them obsessed, absorbing their attention.

clue.text: Salt once ruined main dish when entertaining Major perhaps

indicators.note: entertaining guests means taking them in, so the jumbled letters hold the PM
something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: John Major was Prime Minister, a PM

explanation.surface: A main course was spoilt while hosting a major guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns MAIN DISH into MIDSHIAN; 'entertaining' puts PM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt is a sailor; a midshipman was a junior naval rank held by young officers in training.

clue.text: Trim fruit by mouth

indicators.note: by mouth means spoken, so the word is as it sounds when said

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Cutting back on fruit eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to cut away the outer edge, as you would peel or shave something down.

clue.text: Threesome having time off, Jurgen's agreed to get wine

indicators.note: off means removed, so the time letter is taken away

parts.note: a trio is a threesome
a German name, so the yes is ja

explanation.surface: Three friends on time off, with German Jurgen agreeing, go out for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes T out of TRIO, leaving RIO; JA is German for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of that name.

clue.text: Archdeacon taking a short break returned on a personal vessel

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so these letters are read the other way

parts.note: vac, short for vacation, is a break

explanation.surface: A clergyman came back from a brief holiday on his own boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns VAC into CAV. 'vessel' suggests a boat but means a blood vessel in one's own body.
explanation.definitionFit: This great vein carries blood back to the heart, a blood vessel inside each person.

clue.text: Patrick regularly observed quality of rainbow

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Patrick often looked at a rainbow's colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of 'Patrick' are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is seen as a curved band, so its visible shape is a curve.

clue.text: British actor requires no drop of Drambuie before performing

indicators.note: says the shortened word comes before the stage word
no means without, so a letter comes out

parts.note: needs means requires

indicators.note: a drop of a drink is a tiny amount, here its first letter

parts.note: a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: An actor needs no Drambuie before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' with 'drop of' removes D, the first letter of Drambuie, from NEEDS, leaving NEES. Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam Neeson is a Northern Irish film actor, holding British as well as Irish citizenship.

clue.text: Spy cracked revolutionary mind

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A spy broke a revolutionary's mind under interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' turns SPY into PSY.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or spirit, the seat of thought and feeling.

clue.text: File transferred to PC bust youngster stealing ring

parts.note: a computer that is down is bust, not working

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the youngster holds the ring

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boy who stole a ring is caught when his computer is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' puts O inside LAD to give LOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A download is data copied from the internet or a server onto a home computer.
